mainTopic: Whether growths (גידולין) cancel out a forbidden original plant (עיקר), using onions in שביעית, טבל seeds that were planted, and an onion of תרומה that was planted
overview: The גמרא finishes quoting a משנה about onions that sprouted after rain: if their leaves came out black they are forbidden, and if the leaves turned green they are permitted. It asks why the onions should be forbidden, since the original onion was permitted. The answer is that the משנה forbids only the new growth, not the original onion. The גמרא then asks what רבן שמעון בן גמליאל adds in a ברייתא, since he seems to say the same thing. It answers that the whole משנה is his view. It also adds a rule: when a person actively plants (טרח), the original is cancelled by the majority (בטל ברוב). This rule is challenged from a planted ליטרא of untithed מעשר, which still needs tithing. The answer is that מעשר is a special case based on the פסוק עשר תעשר. Finally, the גמרא returns to רבי ינאי's ruling that a planted onion of תרומה is permitted once its growths exceed the original. It begins to question that ruling, and the question continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the quoted משנה about onions after rain
steps.stepSummary: The quoted משנה ends: if the onions' leaves are black they are forbidden, and if the leaves turned green they are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If their leaves were black, the onions are forbidden. If the leaves turned green, they are permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its quote of a משנה about onions that sprouted after rain. It is setting up the challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Black leaves show strong new growth, and the משנה says that makes the onions forbidden. Green leaves show weaker growth, and those onions stay permitted. The question about to be asked is why the original permitted onion does not stay permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: They turned green, meaning pale and weaker

phrases.aramaic: אִם הָיוּ עָלִין שֶׁלָּהֶן שְׁחוֹרִין — אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: If their leaves were black — they are forbidden,
phrases.notes: This is the end of a משנה about onions that rain fell on and that started to sprout.

phrases.english: if they turned green — they are permitted.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Onions with black leaves are forbidden; onions whose leaves turned green are permitted.

steps.title: Why should black-leaved onions be forbidden?
steps.stepSummary: The original onion was permitted. So why should the onions be forbidden? Where did the permitted part go?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the leaves are black, why are the onions forbidden? Let us say: the permitted part in them, where did it go?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה. It asks why the onions should be forbidden when the original onion itself was permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The original onion grew in a permitted time. The challenge asks where that permitted part disappeared to, since it should still count as permitted. The ruling that everything is forbidden seems hard to explain.

phrases.english: And if they are black, why are they forbidden?
Let us say: the permitted part in them, where did it go?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the ruling of the משנה just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that black-leaved onions are forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The original onion was permitted, so its permitted status should not simply vanish and leave the whole onion forbidden.

steps.title: Only the new growth is forbidden
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the משנה is not forbidding the original onion. It forbids only the added new growth.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Do you think the משנה is talking about the original onion? It teaches that the added growth is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The challenge is answered by rereading the משנה. The word 'forbidden' refers only to the new growth, not to the original onion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the משנה forbids the whole onion, including the original part. Once 'forbidden' is read as referring only to the additional growth, the original stays permitted. Nothing disappeared.

keyTerms.meaning: The original root part of the plant

phrases.english: He said to him: Do you think
phrases.notes: This is רב חסדא answering רבה.

phrases.english: that it teaches about the original part?
It teaches 'forbidden' about the added growth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: מִי סָבְרַתְּ עַל עִיקָּר קָתָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by narrowing what the משנה forbids.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereading the scope of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה forbids the entire onion, including the original.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the new growth is forbidden; the original onion is untouched.

steps.title: Then what does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל add?
steps.stepSummary: If the משנה forbids only the new growth, then רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's ruling in a ברייתא says exactly the same thing. What is he adding?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, what does רבן שמעון בן גמליאל come to say? As a ברייתא teaches: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says, what grew during the time of obligation is obligated, and what grew during the time of exemption is exempt. The תנא קמא also said this!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 3. If that answer is right, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל seems to be repeating the first opinion for no reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן שמעון בן גמליאל splits the plant: growth from the obligated time is obligated, and growth from the exempt time is exempt. That is exactly how Step 3 read the משנה. Since he sounds like he is arguing, the two opinions should differ, but now they appear identical.

keyTerms.meaning: What does he come to say?
What grew during a time of obligation / exemption

phrases.english: If so, what does he come
Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel, to say?

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל אוֹמֵר:
phrases.english: As it is taught: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel says:
What grew during obligation — is obligated,
what grew during exemption — is exempt.
The first tanna also said this!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי, מַאי אֲתָא רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל לְמֵימַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the משנה forbids only the new growth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: That reading makes the תנא קמא and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל say the same thing, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל would be adding nothing.

steps.title: The whole משנה is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, and effort matters
steps.stepSummary: The whole משנה is רבן שמעון בן גמליאל's view, so there is no argument. He keeps the original separate only when the person did not work to plant it. When he did put in effort, the original is cancelled by the majority.
steps.simpleTranslation: The whole משנה is taught by רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. And you only heard רבן שמעון בן גמליאל say this where the person did not exert himself. But where he exerted himself, the original is cancelled by the majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that there is no argument at all, because the משנה itself follows רבן שמעון בן גמליאל. It then adds a distinction: whether the person actively planted makes a difference.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the משנה and the ברייתא share one author, the repetition is no longer a problem. The onions in the משנה sprouted from rain without any human effort, so there the original stays separate. When someone actively plants, the original is cancelled by the larger growth (בטל ברוב), which fits the view that the original gets cancelled.

keyTerms.meaning: You only heard him say this in such a case

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, growth that came by itself stays split between its parts. When a person actively plants, the original is cancelled by the majority of new growth.
steps.confusionAlert: Step 3's reading is kept. The new point is that it applies only when nobody planted. Planting by a person changes the outcome.

phrases.english: The entire mishna

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָתָנֵי לַהּ.
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel teaches it.
And you only heard

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל דְּלָא קָא טָרַח,
phrases.english: Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel say this where he did not exert himself,
phrases.notes: Here the onions just sprouted from the rain, and nobody planted them.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּקָא טָרַח — בָּטֵיל בְּרוּבָּא.
phrases.english: but where he exerted himself — it is cancelled by the majority.

steps.triggerLanguage: כּוּלָּהּ מַתְנִיתִין רַבָּן שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָתָנֵי לַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 4 and adds a new effort-based distinction.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Assigning the משנה to one author plus a distinction between cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה and רבן שמעון בן גמליאל argue, so his words must add something.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are one opinion. The original stays separate only without effort; with planting, it is cancelled by the majority.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the rule of טרח (active planting) that the rest of the סוגיא tests.

steps.title: Challenge from a planted ליטרא of טבל
steps.stepSummary: Is the original always cancelled when someone plants it? A teaching about a planted ליטרא of untithed מעשר says he must still separate for that ליטרא from elsewhere.
steps.simpleTranslation: And anywhere he exerts himself, is the original cancelled by the majority? But there is the case of a ליטרא of untithed מעשר, where he did exert himself, and it teaches: for that ליטרא he must separate מעשר from another place, in proportion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the new rule from Step 5. It brings a case where someone planted and the original was still not cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Planting untithed produce is clearly active effort. Even so, the teaching requires separating מעשר for the original amount from other produce. That means the original was not cancelled by the growth.

keyTerms.meaning: A ליטרא, a measure of weight
מעשר produce that has not yet been properly tithed
From another place, meaning from other produce
According to the calculation, in proportion

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּקָא טָרַח בָּטֵיל בְּרוּבָּא?
phrases.english: And anywhere that he exerts himself, is it cancelled by the majority?
But there is a litra of untithed tithe, where he exerts himself,
phrases.notes: He took that untithed amount and planted it in the ground.

phrases.english: and it teaches: And for that litra

phrases.aramaic: מְעַשֵּׂר עָלָיו מִמָּקוֹם אַחֵר לְפִי חֶשְׁבּוֹן!
phrases.english: he tithes for it from another place, according to the calculation!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּקָא טָרַח בָּטֵיל בְּרוּבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the rule from Step 5 against another source.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that active planting makes the original בטל ברוב
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the planted טבל case there was effort, but the original ליטרא still needs tithing, so it was not cancelled.

steps.title: מעשר is a special case
steps.stepSummary: מעשר is different because of the פסוק 'עשר תעשר'. People normally plant permitted, tithed seeds, not forbidden untithed ones.
steps.simpleTranslation: מעשר is different, because the פסוק says 'You shall surely tithe...'. People sow permitted seed; people do not sow forbidden seed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the טבל case is an exception. מעשר follows its own rule, so it does not disprove the general rule from Step 5.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about tithing what you sow refers to the normal case, permitted seed, which people commonly plant. Planting untithed seed is unusual, so that case is handled differently and the original is not cancelled. The general rule about planting still stands.

phrases.english: It is different with regard to tithe,
as the verse says: 'You shall surely tithe, etc.',
and permitted seed — people sow,
forbidden seed — people do not sow.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers Step 6 by treating מעשר as an exception.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The planted טבל case shows that planting never cancels the original.
steps.terutzMaskana: מעשר is an exception because of how the פסוק and normal human practice work; the general rule about planting remains.

steps.title: Back to רבי ינאי: a planted onion of תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the statement it quoted earlier: an onion of תרומה that was planted and grew more than its original size is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returning to the matter itself: רבי חנינא תירתאה said in the name of רבי ינאי: an onion of תרומה that someone planted, and its growths became more than its original part, is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: With 'גופא', the גמרא goes back to examine רבי ינאי's statement on its own. It is setting up questions about that statement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here a person planted the onion, which is active effort, and the new growth outweighs the original. רבי ינאי rules the whole onion permitted, so the תרומה original is cancelled by the majority.

keyTerms.meaning: Its growths became more than its original part

phrases.english: Returning to the matter itself: Rabbi Ḥanina Tirta'a said
that Rabbi Yannai said:
An onion of teruma that one planted,
and its growths exceeded its original — is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא תִּירְתָּאָה אָמַר רַבִּי יַנַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side discussion and returns to the main statement under study.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A planted onion of תרומה whose growths exceed the original is permitted.

steps.title: Starting to question רבי ינאי's ruling
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to ask what רבי ינאי's ruling implies about growths. The question continues past this point.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is this to say that growths...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts to draw a conclusion from רבי ינאי's ruling so it can test it. The sentence is cut off here and continues in the next part of the דף.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'למימרא' means 'is this to say', which is how the גמרא opens an inference that it plans to question. Here it begins to ask what the ruling shows about the status of growths.

phrases.english: Is this to say that growths

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins to examine רבי ינאי's ruling from Step 8.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ינאי's ruling about the planted onion of תרומה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The גמרא begins to draw an implication about growths from the ruling in order to test it; the full challenge continues beyond this text.
